name: Preparing for Your Real Estate Closing in Collier County: A Step-by-Step Guide

step.name: Step 1: Confirm "Clear to Close" Status
step.text: Work with your lender to ensure your financing is fully approved and you've received the "clear to close." This means all conditions have been met, and the lender is ready to fund your loan. Verify any remaining documentation or signatures needed from you.

step.name: Step 2: Review Your Closing Disclosure
step.text: This is a super important document from your lender, typically received three business days before closing. Review it carefully for accuracy on loan terms, fees, and credits. If anything looks off, raise it immediately with your real estate agent or the settlement agent.

step.name: Step 3: Arrange for Final Funds and Identification
step.text: Your settlement agent will tell you the exact amount of funds needed for closing. This is usually in the form of a wire transfer, so plan ahead for bank cut-off times. You'll also need valid government-issued identification, as well as any other specific documents the title company requests.

step.name: Step 4: Conduct the Final Walkthrough
step.text: Typically scheduled within 24 hours of closing, this is your chance to verify the property is in the agreed-upon condition. Check for agreed-upon repairs, ensure all appliances are working, and confirm no new damage has occurred. If you find issues, report them immediately.

step.name: Step 5: Understand Key Release and Recording
step.text: At closing, you'll sign all the legal documents. Funds will be disbursed, and the deed will be recorded with the county. Only after recording is complete will keys typically be released, officially transferring possession. Understand this timing so you know when you can move in. Navigating these final steps in Collier County with expert coordination ensures nothing gets missed. Contact Kelby Contreras to streamline your real estate closing.
